semantic_correction.stem: A nurse teaches a client how to check moles for warning signs of melanoma. Which assessment follows the ABCDE approach?

options.A: Focus on whether a lesion is painful and use discomfort as the main sign that a mole needs evaluation.
options.B: Assess asymmetry, border irregularity, color variation, diameter, and whether the lesion is evolving over time.
options.C: Focus on color variation and disregard size, shape, border features, or change when assessing a mole.
options.D: Evaluate lesions larger than 6 mm and disregard smaller lesions even when they are changing in appearance.

semantic_correction.rationale: The American Academy of Dermatology describes the ABCDE warning signs of melanoma as Asymmetry, irregular or poorly defined Border, varying Color, Diameter, and Evolving change. AAD notes that melanomas are often greater than 6 mm when diagnosed but can be smaller, so diameter is not an absolute cutoff. Pain is also not required; melanoma may occur without pain or discomfort. Therefore option B correctly applies the complete ABCDE approach.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Teach clients to use the ABCDE approach—Asymmetry, Border, Color, Diameter, and Evolving change—to recognize skin lesions that warrant professional evaluation for possible melanoma.
semantic_correction.source_document_title: Skin cancer types: Melanoma Signs and symptoms
semantic_correction.source_version_date: Current AAD web guidance, copyright 2026; accessed August 21, 2026
semantic_correction.source_locator: The ABCDEs of melanoma — A: one half unlike the other; B: irregular/scalloped/poorly defined border; C: varying colors; D: melanomas usually >6 mm when diagnosed but can be smaller; E: different from other spots or changing in size, shape, or color. Does melanoma hurt? — melanoma can occur without pain or discomfort
semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: AAD identifies Asymmetry, Border irregularity, Color variation, Diameter, and Evolving change as melanoma warning signs, explicitly notes melanomas can be smaller than 6 mm, and states pain is not required.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: removed repeated 'only' distractor cueing, retained the complete ABCDE construct, and made the diameter distractor clinically accurate enough to test the key nuance that melanoma can be smaller than 6 mm.

audit_findings_append.source_locator: Current Melanoma Signs and Symptoms — ABCDEs and pain section
audit_findings_append.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance — preventive skin-cancer education
audit_findings_append.finding: The revised item directly tests the full ABCDE approach without absolute distractor wording or an incorrect 6-mm exclusion rule.

option_audit.A: Incorrect. Melanoma may be painless; pain alone is not the ABCDE screening framework.
option_audit.B: Correct. It reproduces all five AAD ABCDE warning categories.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Color is only one element; asymmetry, border, diameter, and evolution also matter.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. AAD states melanoma can be smaller than 6 mm, especially when evolving or otherwise suspicious.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. B alone contains the complete and current AAD ABCDE framework.
cueing_check: All four options are mole-assessment strategies of comparable length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies B.
